steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Period Study (Paper 1) is worth 50% of the GCSE and lasts 1 hour 30 minutes

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: It focuses on narrative, causation, and change and continuity across a broad chronological period

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: You must know the key events in chronological order — timeline knowledge is essential

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Narrative questions ask you to tell the story of events — use chronological structure

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What percentage of the GCSE is the Period Study worth? | Q: What is the difference between a long-term cause and a trigger cause? | Q: How should you structure a narrative answer?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: 50% — it is Paper 1 and is equally weighted with the Depth Study. | A long-term cause builds up over time, creating the conditions for an event; a trigger cause is the specific event that directly sets it off. | Chronologically, linking events together with causal connectives like 'this led to', 'as a result', and 'consequently'.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: For narrative questions, use dates as structural markers: 'In 490 BCE...', 'By 480 BCE...' In causation answers, group causes into long-term and short-term, then identify which was most significant and why For change and continuity, create a before-and-after comparison in your plan Don't just write about one event in isolation — show how events connect across the period Use the wording of the question to frame every paragraph — keep linking back to it
